_readme: S4 baseline, measured 2026-08-27 against a dead backend. Per surface: failure sentences a person reads for ONE dead read, Try again controls, control shapes a screen reader cannot name, and prose lines past 76ch or capped inline in pixels. check-motion.sh diffs against this and prints REGRESSED or IMPROVED.
_measured_at: 2026-08-27. Signed-in set and public set each re-taken in ONE pass after the station-strip fix. Whole file is one instrument.
_note: Several surfaces have fixes on lane branches that had not merged when this was taken. Where a number looks high, check the lane before treating it as current.
_this_is_a_direction_not_a_target: MATCHING YOUR BASELINE DOES NOT MEAN A SURFACE IS CORRECT. These are the numbers the product happened to produce on one night, several of them from surfaces whose fixes were sitting unmerged on a lane branch. A measurement is a fair way to choose what to fix FIRST. It is not a fair way to decide what the thing should BE, and a baseline is the exact shape that quietly turns one into the other. Read the LIST the report prints, not the number, and lower a baseline entry whenever a real fix lands rather than treating the old value as the goal. Founder's correction, relayed 2026-08-27.
_the_zeros_need_reading_not_celebrating: /plan, /ship and /inbox score 0. That is NOT automatically good. Their previous 1 was entirely the station strip's 'count unavailable', so with a dead backend they now say NOTHING about their own failed reads. Silence on failure is the /proof shape: a person cannot tell 'nothing to show' from 'we could not look'. A zero here is a prompt to open the screenshot, exactly like a rise is.
